<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918472_theRebbe_445" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918472_theRebbe_445__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening header with date and location for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven*.</t>
    <t s="1">Motzaei Shabbat Kodesh Parshat Emor,</t>
    <t s="2">13 Iyar*</t>
    <t s="3">*,</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Date of Pesach Sheni, 14 Iyar 5738.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Night of 14 Iyar,</t>
    <t s="1">Pesach Sheni,</t>
    <t s="2">5738</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains Pesach Sheni through three introductions: the difference between the first and second months in divine service and in the Sefiros, and the concept of Pesach as a leap.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">To understand the concept of Pesach Sheni,</t>
    <t s="1">and the Tzemach Tzedek explains in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"1,</t>
    <t s="2">that the concept of Pesach Sheni will be understood based on three introductions.</t>
    <t s="3">The first introduction is the difference between the first month</t>
    <t s="4">(Nissan)</t>
    <t s="5">and the second month</t>
    <t s="6">(Iyar)</t>
    <t s="7">in the service of man.</t>
    <t s="8">For in the month of Nissan,</t>
    <t s="9">whose focal point is the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="10">it is the service of "turn away from evil,"</t>
    <t s="11">meaning that evil is in its full strength and the service is to turn away from evil,</t>
    <t s="12">to go out and flee from evil,</t>
    <t s="13">itkafya2.</t>
    <t s="14">And the service of the month of Iyar</t>
    <t s="15">[whose unique aspect, by which it is distinguished from the other months, is that on each of its days there is a specific mitzvah</t>
    <t s="16">(of Sefiras HaOmer)3]</t>
    <t s="17">is the service of Sefiras HaOmer,</t>
    <t s="18">whose concept is4</t>
    <t s="19">the refinement of the midos and their transformation to holiness,</t>
    <t s="20">it'hapcha.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is what is said5</t>
    <t s="22">"On the first of the second month... of their going out from the land of Egypt,"</t>
    <t s="23">that the first service of the Exodus,</t>
    <t s="24">the first month,</t>
    <t s="25">is itkafya of the sitra achara,</t>
    <t s="26">and afterwards comes the service of it'hapcha,</t>
    <t s="27">the second service of the Exodus,</t>
    <t s="28">the second month6.</t>
    <t s="29">And the second introduction is the distinction between these two months regarding the Sefiros.</t>
    <t s="30">For the first month is in Malchus,</t>
    <t s="31">the first Sefirah from below upward,</t>
    <t s="32">and the second month is in Yesod,</t>
    <t s="33">the second Sefirah7.</t>
    <t s="34">And it is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="35">that these two introductions</t>
    <t s="36">[their concept of Nissan and Iyar in the service of man,</t>
    <t s="37">and their concept in the Sefiros]</t>
    <t s="38">are related to each other,</t>
    <t s="39">as explained in Torah Ohr, the maamar beginning "And behold we were binding sheaves"8</t>
    <t s="40">that the refinement through the tribes</t>
    <t s="41">(who were a chariot for the aspect of Malchus),</t>
    <t s="42">the first refinement,</t>
    <t s="43">is only the nullification of the yesh</t>
    <t s="44">(analogous to itkafya9),</t>
    <t s="45">and the refinement through Yosef HaTzaddik,</t>
    <t s="46">the aspect of Yesod,</t>
    <t s="47">the second refinement,</t>
    <t s="48">is that it be included in Elokus,</t>
    <t s="49">nullification in actual existence</t>
    <t s="50">(analogous to it'hapcha9).</t>
    <t s="51">And the third introduction is,</t>
    <t s="52">that the concept of Pesach,</t>
    <t s="53">Pesach from the term skipping and jumping10,</t>
    <t s="54">is a most lofty drawing down that cannot come through the order of hishtalshelus and only by way of a leap,</t>
    <t s="55">as explained in Likkutei Torah11.</t>
    <t s="56">And it is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="57">that from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="58">that also the concept of Pesach Sheni12</t>
    <t s="59">is a leap,</t>
    <t s="60">a drawing down that is above hishtalshelus.</t>
    <t s="61">And the difference between the first Pesach and Pesach Sheni is in the place and the concept in which this drawing down is drawn.</t>
    <t s="62">For by the first Pesach it is written13</t>
    <t s="63">"And Pesach to Hashem on the entrance,"</t>
    <t s="64">that the drawing down by way of a leap</t>
    <t s="65">(and Pesach)</t>
    <t s="66">was at the entrance,</t>
    <t s="67">the Sefirah of Malchus14,</t>
    <t s="68">and in the soul of man – in yirah tata'ah</t>
    <t s="69">("This is the gate to Hashem"15)</t>
    <t s="70">which is the root of "turn away from evil"16,</t>
    <t s="71">and the drawing down by way of a leap that is in Pesach Sheni is in the Sefirah of Yesod,</t>
    <t s="72">whose concept in the soul of man is connection and love17,</t>
    <t s="73">through which his midos are transformed to holiness,</t>
    <t s="74">it'hapcha.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
